name: REF_lower3
description: Anchor: framework defaults (net-loss trigger, 3% off loss exit, frozen-high 95% reset). Equals the existing 3% strategy trade for trade (calibration gate).
hypothesis: Reference leg for every ablation table; identical to lower-price-reentry B_lower_3pct.

name: G_A2m1
description: A2_material_1 trigger alone (price return <= -1% arms; else no restriction); level/reset = REF. Exact copy of loss-classification material_trigger(0.01).
hypothesis: Ablation leg. Targets the micro-arming failure (a trivial loss blocking a recovery winner) by never arming on immaterial losses. Family A: QQQ-old +26.9k net / -13.1k DD vs A0; expected to reproduce A2_material_1 exactly (cross-family integrity check).

name: G_D7tiny
description: D7_tiny_loss_exit_anchor alone: alt entry when |arming net loss| < $2,000 AND close <= frozen loss-exit price; level/reset = REF. Verbatim copy from recovery-opportunities/strategies.py.
hypothesis: Ablation leg. Same micro-arming failure as G_A2m1 but the opposite philosophy: arm gently (hold the exit-price line) instead of never arming — Family E found micro-armings are often net positive, so the gentle anchor should keep their benefits. Expected to reproduce Family D results exactly (integrity check).

name: G_B7stall
description: B7_stall level alone: discount 3% while the episode low is < 20 sessions old, then linear decay to 0 over 60 sessions; trigger/reset = REF. Verbatim copy from adaptive-discounts b7_stall.
hypothesis: Ablation leg. Targets the stale-grind failure (QQQ 2003 basing: the frozen 3% level is never printed once the low stops falling). Family B: trade-identical to 3% on three datasets, QQQ-old +21.2k/-21.2k. Expected identical here.

name: G_B2inv
description: B2_inverse level alone: discount = clip(3% - 0.5*|price return|, 0.5%, 3%) off the loss exit; trigger/reset = REF. Verbatim copy from adaptive-discounts b2_inverse.
hypothesis: Ablation leg. Targets the V-bottom-miss failure after severe losses (the market already delivered the decline; demanding 3% more prices us out at capitulation). Family B: better on 3 of 4, -38.6k QQQ-new from early re-entries after big 2022/2025 losses. Expected identical.

name: G_C6r38
description: C6_retrace_38 reset alone: reset when close >= low + 0.38*(frozen ref high - low); trigger/level = REF. Verbatim copy from recovery-resets retrace_reset(0.38).
hypothesis: Ablation leg. Targets reset obsolescence (frozen-high 95% unreachable in deep bears) with a depth-adaptive reset. Family C: best aggregate (+56k over C1), rescued VGT 2023-01 and half of QQQ 2003; cost -3.4k VGT-old. Expected identical.

name: G_C11grad
description: C11_graduated alone: 3% discount until the close has reached 1.08x the episode low (sticky), then 1.5%; frozen95 reset. Verbatim copy from recovery-resets graduated_level.
hypothesis: Ablation leg. Targets sub-2% near-miss failures on W-shaped retests (rebound confirmation buys a smaller discount). Family C: never below C1, +16.2k/+15.2k old era, 2000-02 window positive. Expected identical.

name: G2_tiny_stall
description: Level: |net loss| < $2,000 => frozen loss-exit price (D7_tiny anchor); else B7_stall decayed 3% level. Net-loss trigger, C1 frozen95 reset.
hypothesis: Two DISTINCT failure mechanisms, one component each: D7_tiny fixes micro-armings (tiny losses demand only "no higher than the exit", preserving blocked recovery winners like QQQ 2010-08 and VGT-new micro episodes) while B7_stall fixes stale grinds (QQQ 2003 basing re-admission). They act on disjoint episode sets (tiny vs non-tiny), so gains should be ~additive: QQQ-old from both, VGT/QQQ-new mostly from the tiny branch. Risk: none new — each component keeps the full 3% exactly where the other is inactive.

name: G3_tiny_retrace
description: Level: tiny => loss-exit anchor, else fixed 3%; reset = C6_retrace_38. Net-loss trigger.
hypothesis: Micro-arming fix (D7_tiny, entry side) + obsolescence fix (C6 retrace reset, exit-of-restriction side). Distinct state variables (arming loss size vs episode depth), so overlaps only where a tiny episode would also reset early — the retrace level of a shallow episode is low, so C6 may fire before the tiny anchor is ever touched, making the combo sub-additive on tiny episodes but still additive on deep ones (2003, 2023-01). Risk: C6 false resets in 2000-02 bear rallies now clear episodes the tiny anchor would have held cheaply.

name: G4_A2m1_stall
description: Trigger: A2_material_1 (price return <= -1% arms, else none); level = B7_stall; reset = C1.
hypothesis: The never-arm counterpart of G2: A2m1 removes micro-armings entirely (no restriction to relax) while B7_stall handles stale grinds on the material episodes that do arm. Head-to-head with G2 this is the cleanest never-arm vs arm-gently comparison inside an identical second component. Risk (from Family E): exempted micro-losses were often net POSITIVE restrictions (2026-02-05 +21.9k), so G4 may give back new-era gains that G2 keeps.

name: G5_tiny_stall_retrace
description: The full stack: level = tiny => exit anchor else B7_stall decay; reset = C6_retrace_38; net-loss trigger.
hypothesis: All three distinct fixes at once (micro-armings / stale grinds / reset obsolescence). The test is whether B7_stall and C6_retrace_38 overlap: both activate in long episodes where the low has stopped falling — the stall decay lowers the entry bar while the retrace reset clears the episode; whichever fires first makes the other redundant in that episode. Expect G5 ~ G3 where C6 fires early and ~ G2 where the decay wins; if G5 < max(G2, G3) per dataset the components interfere (a C6 reset surrendering a decayed-level pending entry).

name: G6_stall_grad
description: Double-relaxation test: discount = min(d_stall(age of low), d_graduated(8% rebound, sticky)) off the loss exit; C1 reset; net-loss trigger.
hypothesis: Hypothesis to TEST, stated in advance: redundant or harmful. Both components relax on "stabilization" via different observables (low age vs rebound off the low); min() takes the looser at every session, so in bear rallies that both (a) rebound 8% and (b) pause new lows 20+ sessions, the requirement collapses faster than either alone — re-admitting 2001-02 rally entries. Expected: bear windows worse than both legs; any gain over the better leg would refute redundancy.

name: G7_tiny_grad
description: Level: tiny => loss-exit anchor; else C11_graduated staged discount (3% -> 1.5% after an 8% rebound, sticky); C1 reset; net-loss trigger.
hypothesis: Micro-arming fix + W-retest fix: distinct mechanisms on distinct episodes (tiny episodes need no rebound confirmation; material episodes get C11's confirmed-rebound relaxation that was never below C1 anywhere in Family C). The most conservative combo: nothing relaxes below 1.5% and only after a confirmed 8% rebound. Expect C11's old-era gains plus D7's new-era gains with no new bear risk.

name: G8_A2m1_retrace
description: Trigger: A2_material_1; level = fixed 3%; reset = C6_retrace_38.
hypothesis: Never-arm micro fix + adaptive reset. A2m1 removes the micro episodes; C6 shortens the deep ones. Distinct episode sets again, but C6's rescue of VGT 2023-01 came indirectly via extra Nov-Dec 2022 trades whose losses were small — if A2m1 declines those armings the two components could CANCEL rather than add (the extra trades change which exits anchor later levels). This combo tests precisely that interaction.

name: G9a_retrace_guard
description: C6_retrace_38 reset gated by the reset guard: reset may fire ONLY if close > required level x 1.02 (fixed 3% level => guard constant exit*0.9894); standard trigger, fixed 3% discount.
hypothesis: Family C's inversion fix: a permissive reset can fire while the close sits at/below the pending required level, surrendering a discount entry the restriction had already earned (reset priority). The guard forbids resets in that zone. Binds only when the 38% retrace point sits <= exit*0.9894 (episode low more than ~21% below ref high, deep episodes). Expect: identical to G_C6r38 in shallow episodes; in deep bears the guard converts early resets into held discounts — better 2000-02/2008 entries or no change; it cannot create new entries.

name: G9b_exitreset_guard
description: Diagnostic: C2-style reset (close >= frozen loss-exit price) WITH the same guard (close > exit*0.97*1.02). Standard trigger, fixed 3% discount.
hypothesis: Does the guard rescue an otherwise catastrophic permissive reset (Family C: QQQ 2000-02 -57,079, DD 114,608)? Analytic expectation stated BEFORE running: NO — exit >= exit*0.9894 always, so the guard never binds and G9b should be trade-identical to unguarded C2. C2's failure mechanism is not the inversion (its resets fire ABOVE the pending level by construction); it is re-admission at unimproved prices. The run is the empirical confirmation, and the pair (G9a, G9b) separates "guard fixes inversion" from "guard fixes permissiveness".

name: G10_bimodal
description: Loss-magnitude bimodal level: |net loss| < $2,000 => frozen loss-exit price; else B2_inverse discount clip(3% - 0.5*|price return|, 0.5%, 3%). C1 reset; net-loss trigger.
hypothesis: One idea at both ends of the loss distribution: tiny losses need no discount (micro-arming fix), severe losses already delivered their discount (V-bottom capitulation fix); mid-size losses keep ~the full 3%. Components share the exit anchor but partition by loss size, so no within-episode interaction. Risk carried in from B2_inverse: early re-entries after big 2022/2025 QQQ losses (-38.6k QQQ-new) — the tiny branch does nothing to offset that.
